title: Paccheri with Ragu
subtitle: Large pasta tubes with a slow beef and tomato sauce
excerpt: Wide tube pasta filled and coated in a slow-cooked beef ragu. The long cooking time is most of the work: the sauce needs at least 2 hours to develop its depth.
sourceNotes: Paccheri al ragu is a Neapolitan-style pasta dish using large tube pasta common in southern Italian cooking.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the ragu alone for up to 3 months. Cook fresh pasta to serve.
recipe.batchNotes: The ragu doubles and triples well. Use a wide, heavy-based pot and keep the heat low.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The ragu improves over 24 to 48 hours in the fridge. Reheat gently on the hob.

content.text: Paccheri with ragu is a weekend dish that rewards patience. The ragu needs a very low, unhurried simmer of at least 2 hours. Do not try to rush it by raising the heat or the mince will go grainy instead of melting into the sauce.
Heat the oil in a heavy-based pot over a medium heat. Add the onion, carrot, and celery. Cook for 10 minutes until soft and lightly golden.
Add the garlic. Cook for 1 minute. Raise the heat to high and add the beef mince. Break it up with a spoon. Cook for 8 minutes until fully browned.
Pour in the red wine. Scrape the base of the pan. Simmer until the wine has almost evaporated, about 3 minutes.
Add the tomato puree and stir for 1 minute. Add the tinned tomatoes, bay leaves, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Reduce the heat to low. Cook uncovered for 2 hours, stirring every 20 minutes. The sauce should be thick and glossy.
Cook the paccheri in well-salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve a mugful of pasta water. Drain the pasta.
Remove the bay leaves. Toss the pasta in the ragu with a splash of pasta water. Serve with grated parmesan.

items.symptom: The ragu is catching on the bottom of the pan.
items.cause: The heat is too high for the long simmer.
items.fix: Drop the heat to its lowest setting. Add a splash of water and stir. A diffuser mat helps on gas hobs.

items.symptom: The sauce tastes watery and thin after 2 hours.
items.cause: Too much liquid was added or the heat was too low to reduce.
items.fix: Remove the lid and raise the heat slightly. Simmer for a further 20 to 30 minutes uncovered.

items.symptom: The paccheri tubes are sticking together.
items.cause: They were drained and left to sit without sauce.
items.fix: Toss them into the ragu immediately after draining and add pasta water to keep them moving.
